title: New Flip Phone Made to Do 'as Little as Possible'
paragraphs: Most smartphone companies want people to spend as much time as possible on their devices. However, one company has designed a new phone with the opposite goal in mind.

The device, called the Light Phone Flip, was announced in 2026 by Light, a technology company based in Brooklyn, New York. According to the company, the phone is "designed to be used as little as possible." It is Light's fourth device and its first flip phone, which means it folds closed like a clamshell.

Unlike modern folding smartphones, the Light Phone Flip has no touchscreen, no flexible display and no screen on the outside. Instead, it has a small 2.8-inch OLED display and a number keypad with physical buttons. Users type messages with predictive T9 text, a method that was common on older mobile phones, or by using voice-to-text. When the phone is closed, a single light shows that there is a notification.

Most importantly, the phone has no social media, no web browser and no grid of apps. Instead, it offers a limited set of basic tools, including calls, messages, alarms, a calculator, a calendar, directions, music, podcasts, notes and weather. It also has a 12-megapixel camera, 5G and Bluetooth, and it has a battery that users can replace themselves.
The phone costs $299 and is available to pre-order, with shipping expected to begin in April 2027.

Light's co-founder, Kaiwei Tang, describes the phone as an alternative to the so-called "attention economy," in which smartphones are increasingly designed to keep users looking at their screens for as long as possible.

The Light Phone Flip is one of several "minimalist" phones aimed at people who want to spend less time on their devices. However, these phones remain a small part of the market, and they may not suit people who depend on smartphone apps for work, banking or travel.
